title: Bilateral Validation of Electrical Promontory Stimulation Under General Anesthesia: A Prospective Exploratory Study
summary:
Electrical auditory nerve stimulation is an established procedure for testing the
function of the auditory nerve in patients with severe hearing loss or deafness, particularly prior to cochlear implantation. It is used to test the function of the auditory nerve through electrical stimulation. A needle electrode is inserted into the (middle) ear, which emits the electrical stimulus.
This test is usually performed routinely under general anesthesia to avoid unwanted reactions from other nerves. In addition, if the test responses are absent or unclear, the electrode positions can be adjusted during the test without causing pain.
However, the validity of this auditory nerve testing under anesthesia is increasingly being questioned. Comparative studies with healthy ears are still largely lacking.
However, the validity of this auditory nerve test under anesthesia is increasingly being questioned. Comparative studies with healthy ears are largely lacking to date.
This is particularly relevant because the test is recommended in the guidelines for cochlear implant diagnostics when indicated—although the measurement results are not considered conclusive evidence, they can still be included in the diagnostic assessment. Therefore, it is imperative to evaluate the test on healthy ears, compare the results with conventional hearing tests, and compare the healthy and affected sides.
conditions: Indications for the implantation of a Cholea implant

interventions.name: Patients > 18 years of age who undergo auditory nerve testing as part of pre-diagnostic testing for cochlear implants . Patients undergo 1-2 times per month auditory nerve testing using the promontory test.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
> 18 years of age who have undergone a promontory test (auditory nerve test) as part of the cochlear implant pre-diagnostics and have given their consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Patients younger than 18 years of age
Patients older than 18 years of age who have not undergone a promontory test (auditory nerve test) and/or who have refused to participate in the study
Patients without a promontory test (auditory nerve test) as part of the pre-diagnostic assessment for cochlear implants
